*   **When not to use:** When the surface requires multiple intersections per edge, as the method averages them into a single vertex [S1].

The claim states that the method should not be used when the surface requires multiple intersections per edge because it averages them into a single vertex. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly describes an ablation ('Subgrid Mod 2') that 'limits output to at most one intersection per edge' and 'calculate[s] the aggregated intersection location for the single output vertex by averaging all true intersection positions found along the edge.' It further notes that this method 'cannot produce more than one disc per tetrahedron' and results in 'much more distortion' compared to the full method that uses all intersections. This supports the claim that averaging multiple intersections into a single vertex is a limitation that degrades quality, implying it is not suitable for cases requiring multiple intersections.
